raw_response:
I would keep it simple and plant the crop pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou, that rotation fits the climate and the local way of farming well. The county has a long frost-free period, most rain comes in summer, and wheat-maize is still the main grain pattern on the North China Plain and in Quzhou. At my age, with no formal schooling, I would not chase a complicated cash crop that needs more market judgment, more labor, and tighter timing. I would rather protect steady grain output, control costs, and avoid taking too much risk.

I would manage the land with moderate fertilizer and careful water use, not with the highest-input approach. Wheat needs the tighter management because spring is drier, so I would irrigate wheat more than maize. I would use improved seed, not expensive specialty seed, and I would stay with familiar field operations: rotary tillage before wheat, then no-till or very light disturbance for maize after wheat harvest to save time and moisture. I would spray only when needed, usually a small number of times for weeds, aphids or disease in wheat, and for weeds plus one pest control round in maize. My goal would be stable yield, lower risk, and work I can actually manage myself through the whole year.
